newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia looks into Ericsson contract.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia looks into Ericsson contract.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Wednesday he has received a report that there may have been "discrepancies" in a contract awarded by Telekom Malaysia Bhd to Sweden's LM Ericcson.
"I have received an internal report that mentioned discrepancies in the tender awarded by Telekom to Ericsson," Anwar told reporters in reply to questions after an official function at his ministry.
He said he has not been able to verify the authenticity of the charges but has submitted the report to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad.
"I've told him (Mahathir) it's going to come out, we are going to have to deal with it and take action if it's true. I can't confirm the authencity of the report," he said.
Anwar, also the Finance Minister, said the information he received was too general to be acted upon.
"We have to do justice to all parties concerned," he said.
Anwar said he has asked Telekom Malaysia to look into matter.
"We have asked them to check all tenders saying procedures should be fully adhered to. We are waiting for more details," he said.
Telekom officials could not be contacted for comment.
Anwar did not say which Ericsson contract was under question.
In Sweden on Wednesday, Ericsson said it had no comment concerning this particular case but suspected it was connected to earlier rumours of criminal and unethical actions.

"We haven't yet been able to confirm what has actually been said but we suspect this has a connection to the rumours spread by a business contact in the Middle East," Ericsson's head of information Lars Stalberg told Reuters in Stockholm.
"These reports have been spread all over the world, including Malaysia."
Ericsson said in a statement on December 20 last year that the company had been the subject of serious allegations concerning deliveries to the Middle East.

"The board of Ericsson has read the report and I want to reject with force all the allegations directed towards Ericsson's actions and individuals in the management", Ericsson's chairman Bjorn Svedberg said then.
In September, the Swedish firm announced it had signed a 960 million crown contract with Telekom Malaysia for delivery of AXE telecommunications systems over two years.
In December, local newspapers reported that Ericsson, U.S.-based Motorola Inc and Japan's NEC Corp were the three bidders for a Telekom contract to set up personal digital cellular network.
